title: AdderNet 2.0: Optimal FPGA Acceleration of AdderNet with Activation-Oriented Quantization and Fused Bias Removal based Memory Optimization
problem: AdderNet accelerators face critical implementation challenges to achieve maximal hardware and energy efficiency on FPGAs. Memory bandwidth and on-chip feature memory bitwidth are significant bottlenecks limiting practical deployment.
motivation: Efficient neural network acceleration matters because CNNs are computationally demanding and energy-efficient alternatives like AdderNet can significantly reduce computation and power consumption.
method: The framework combines three techniques to address memory bottlenecks. Activation-Oriented Quantization (AOQ) analyzes actual computation values and reduces their bitwidth, while Fused Bias Removal (FBR) merges operations to reduce on-chip memory needs. Processing Element designs are optimized for better resource utilization. Multiple configurations are tested on a Xilinx KV-260 FPGA to find the best combination.
key_novelty: Combining Activation-Oriented Quantization (reducing numerical precision based on observed computation values) with Fused Bias Removal (merging the bias term into other computations to reduce on-chip memory bitwidth) simultaneously improves both memory bandwidth and resource efficiency for AdderNet accelerators.
contributions: Activation-Oriented Quantization (AOQ) strategy for AdderNet quantization
Fused Bias Removal (FBR) scheme for on-chip feature memory bitwidth reduction
Optimal PE design methodology for enhanced resource utilization
INT6 AdderNet 2.0 accelerator implementation on Xilinx KV-260 FPGA demonstrating significant gains

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: significant energy savings vs prior designs

limitations: Trade-offs between quantization aggressiveness and accuracy preservation, and applicability to other network architectures beyond AdderNet are not discussed.
primary_theme: FPGA acceleration of efficient neural networks through co-optimized quantization and memory design
